search_objective: Discover authoritative sources reporting Dengue cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Brazil during Q1 2024 (2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31), covering official Brazilian health agency bulletins, international organization situation reports, structured surveillance databases, and high-quality news/media reports.
search_reasoning: Brazil's primary dengue surveillance authority is the Ministério da Saúde (Ministry of Health) and its epidemiological intelligence arm SVSA/SVS, which publishes weekly "Boletim Epidemiológico" and InfoDengue dashboards. Q1 2024 was a historically severe dengue season in Brazil, so PAHO/WHO situation reports and ProMED/HealthMap alerts are also expected to carry quantitative data. Portuguese-language queries are essential because the most granular subnational data (by estado/município) appears in Brazilian government publications in Portuguese. International English-language queries target PAHO, WHO AFRO/AMRO, and global news wires. The upstream planned queries are English-only and use awkward date-range strings as literal search terms; this iteration replaces them with four high-yield, well-formed queries across the four most productive channels within the 4-query-per-iteration budget: (1) Portuguese-language official Brazilian MoH bulletin search, (2) PAHO/WHO AMRO situation report search in English, (3) Portuguese-language InfoDengue/SINAN structured data search, and (4) English-language news/wire search targeting the Q1 2024 outbreak peak.

query_batch.query: boletim epidemiológico dengue Brasil 2024 semana epidemiológica casos óbitos Ministério da Saúde
query_batch.query_rationale: Portuguese is the primary language of Brazilian federal health publications. The Ministério da Saúde publishes weekly dengue bulletins with granular subnational data. Using Brazilian epidemiological terminology ('semana epidemiológica', 'óbitos', 'boletim epidemiológico') maximises recall of the most authoritative primary source. This replaces the upstream English-only q_exec_001/002 with a far more targeted localized query.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde / SVSA) weekly epidemiological bulletin (Boletim Epidemiológico) for dengue, Q1 2024; expected to contain cumulative case counts by epidemiological week, state-level breakdowns, confirmed/probable/suspected classifications, and death counts.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Official .gov.br domain; authorship attributed to SVSA/SVS/Ministério da Saúde; structured tabular data with SE (semana epidemiológica) references.

query_batch.query: PAHO AMRO dengue Brazil 2024 situation report cases deaths epidemiological update Q1
query_batch.query_rationale: PAHO is the primary international validation source for dengue in the Americas. Its situation reports independently corroborate Brazilian MoH figures and often provide cross-country context. This refines upstream q_exec_003/004 by explicitly naming PAHO/AMRO and removing the literal date-range string that would suppress relevant results.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO (Pan American Health Organization) epidemiological alerts, situation reports, or weekly updates on dengue in the Americas covering Brazil Q1 2024; may include cumulative regional totals and country-specific figures.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: paho.int or paho.org domain; PAHO/WHO authorship; structured situation report format with case counts and epidemiological week references.

query_batch.query: dengue Brasil 2024 SINAN InfoDengue casos notificados municípios estados janeiro março
query_batch.query_rationale: SINAN is Brazil's mandatory disease notification system and the most granular subnational data source for dengue. InfoDengue (Fiocruz) provides near-real-time municipal-level estimates. These structured databases are essential for populating subnational_location and locality fields. This replaces the generic upstream q_exec_007/008 with Brazil-specific system names.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: SINAN (Sistema de Informação de Agravos de Notificação) or InfoDengue open-data portal entries for dengue notifications in Brazil Q1 2024; structured tabular or dashboard data with municipality/state granularity.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: datasus.saude.gov.br, infodengue.fiocruz.br, or opendatasus.saude.gov.br domain; Fiocruz or DATASUS authorship; machine-readable or dashboard format.

query_batch.query: Brazil dengue outbreak 2024 record cases deaths emergency January February March
query_batch.query_rationale: Q1 2024 was Brazil's worst dengue season on record, generating extensive international news coverage with quantitative figures. News sources provide independently reported case/death counts that can corroborate official data and may surface subnational hotspot information (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro). This refines upstream q_exec_009/010 by removing the literal date-range string and adding 'record' and 'emergency' to target the historically anomalous outbreak.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: International wire services (Reuters, AP, AFP), major Brazilian English-language outlets (Brazil Reports, The Rio Times), or global health news aggregators (Outbreak News Today, ProMED) reporting on the Q1 2024 Brazil dengue surge with quantitative case/death figures.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Datelines within Jan–Mar 2024; explicit citation of Brazilian MoH or PAHO figures; named journalist or wire byline; quantitative case counts in article body.

expected_evidence: Weekly cumulative dengue case counts (confirmed, probable, suspected) for Brazil by epidemiological week (SE 1–13, 2024)
State-level (UF) case and death breakdowns from Brazilian MoH bulletins
PAHO situation report figures for dengue in Brazil/Americas Q1 2024
SINAN or InfoDengue municipal/state notification counts for Jan–Mar 2024
Death (óbitos) and hospitalization counts from official Brazilian sources
News-reported quantitative figures citing MoH or PAHO as primary source
Declaration of public health emergency (emergência em saúde pública) with associated case thresholds
expected_source_characteristics: Brazilian federal government domain (.gov.br): saude.gov.br, datasus.saude.gov.br
PAHO domain: paho.int or paho.org, AMRO regional office
ProMED-mail or HealthMap alerts with Brazil dengue 2024 posts
International wire services with Jan–Mar 2024 datelines and quantitative case figures
Brazilian Portuguese language publications with 'boletim epidemiológico', 'semana epidemiológica', 'casos notificados', 'óbitos'
language_or_localization_reasoning: Brazil's official dengue surveillance publications are produced exclusively in Brazilian Portuguese by the Ministério da Saúde (SVSA/SVS). The most authoritative and granular sources — weekly Boletins Epidemiológicos, SINAN notifications, and InfoDengue dashboards — use Portuguese terminology: 'dengue', 'casos notificados', 'casos confirmados', 'óbitos', 'semana epidemiológica (SE)', 'municípios', 'estados/UF'. Searching only in English (as the upstream plan did) would miss these primary sources entirely. Two of the four iteration-1 queries are therefore in Portuguese (it1_q1, it1_q3). International validation sources (PAHO, news wires) are queried in English (it1_q2, it1_q4) as those publications are primarily English-language. This bilingual approach maximises recall across both primary Brazilian and international validation source layers.
trust_considerations: Prioritise .gov.br sources (Ministério da Saúde, DATASUS, SVSA) as primary authoritative sources; these carry the highest trust for case counts and deaths.
PAHO situation reports are the primary international validation layer; figures may lag Brazilian MoH by 1–2 weeks but are independently verified.
SINAN/InfoDengue data may be provisional for recent weeks; note any 'dados preliminares' (preliminary data) caveats in evidence quotes.
News sources should only be used where they explicitly cite MoH or PAHO figures; do not treat journalist estimates as primary case counts.
Avoid sources that aggregate without citing primary data (e.g., generic health news blogs without named official source).
Q1 2024 Brazil dengue was declared a public health emergency; sources referencing this declaration are likely to contain quantitative thresholds and are high-value.
stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is insufficient on its own; a second iteration will be needed to cover subnational state-level breakdowns and any ProMED/academic rapid-communication sources. Stop after iteration 2 if official MoH bulletins, PAHO situation reports, and at least one structured database source have been identified.
warnings: The upstream planned queries used literal date-range strings (e.g., '2024-01-01-2024-03-31') as search terms, which would suppress most relevant results; all iteration-1 queries have been rewritten to avoid this.
Upstream queries were English-only; the most granular Brazilian subnational data is published exclusively in Portuguese — Portuguese-language queries (it1_q1, it1_q3) are essential for full coverage.
Brazil's dengue reporting uses epidemiological weeks (semanas epidemiológicas, SE); Q1 2024 corresponds approximately to SE 1–13; evidence quotes should reference SE numbers where possible.
SINAN data for Q1 2024 may still be under revision as of mid-2024; any structured database results should be checked for 'dados preliminares' flags.

The 4-query budget for this iteration is fully consumed; subnational state-specific queries (e.g., São Paulo, Minas Gerais) and ProMED/academic rapid-communication queries are deferred to iteration 2.

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong broad coverage — Brazilian MoH bulletins (gov.br), PAHO situation reports (paho.org), state-level sources (saude.mg.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br, goias.gov.br, cevs.rs.gov.br), InfoDengue (info.dengue.mat.br), and open data (dadosabertos.saude.gov.br) are all represented. However, several critical gaps remain for the specific Q1 2024 (SE 1–13) window: (1) The most directly relevant MoH bulletin found (gov.br, SE 4 snippet) covers only through SE 4; we need the dedicated Q1 2024 dengue bulletin (Boletim Epidemiológico Especial or the COE-Dengue weekly reports for SE 1–13). (2) The PAHO results found are dated June 2024 and October 2024 — no Q1-specific PAHO alert or situation report covering Jan–Mar 2024 has been confirmed. (3) The Minas Gerais and Distrito Federal state bulletins found appear to cover later periods (SE 52/2024, June 2024); Q1-specific state-level data for the highest-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás) is not yet confirmed. (4) The COE-Dengue emergency declaration (February 2024) and associated quantitative thresholds have not been surfaced. (5) ProMED/WHO Disease Outbreak News entries for the Q1 2024 Brazil dengue emergency have not appeared. A second iteration with 4 targeted queries can close these gaps within the allowed budget (10 total queries, 2 iterations max).

query_batch.query: boletim epidemiológico especial dengue 2024 semanas epidemiológicas 1 13 casos óbitos Brasil COE emergência saúde pública
query_batch.query_rationale: The Brazilian MoH/SVSA publishes a dedicated 'Boletim Epidemiológico Especial' for dengue at the end of each season, and also COE-Dengue weekly monitoring reports during the emergency period. Q1 2024 (SE 1–13) is the peak of the outbreak and the period when the public health emergency was declared (~February 2024). This query targets the most authoritative Q1-specific national case/death totals, which were not surfaced in iteration 1 (the gov.br result found covers only through SE 4). The COE (Comitê de Operações de Emergência) terminology is essential as the emergency declaration generated a distinct series of reports.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: SVSA/Ministério da Saúde 'Boletim Epidemiológico Especial Dengue 2024' or COE-Dengue weekly monitoring bulletin covering SE 1–13 (January–March 2024); expected to contain cumulative national case counts (confirmed, probable, suspected), deaths (óbitos), hospitalizations, and state-level (UF) breakdowns for Q1 2024.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: gov.br domain (saude.gov.br or svsa.saude.gov.br); SVSA/SVS authorship; 'Boletim Epidemiológico Especial' or 'COE-Dengue' series label; SE 1–13 reference.
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: it1_q1 — the gov.br bulletin found covers only SE 4; this query targets the Q1-complete or COE-Dengue emergency series

query_batch.query: PAHO dengue Brazil 2024 epidemiological alert January February March cases deaths emergency
query_batch.query_rationale: Iteration 1 returned PAHO results dated June 2024 and October 2024 — neither covers Q1 2024 specifically. PAHO issued at least one epidemiological alert specifically about the Brazil dengue emergency in early 2024 (likely February–March 2024) when Brazil declared a public health emergency. This query explicitly targets the Q1 2024 PAHO alert by adding 'January February March' and 'emergency' to distinguish it from the mid-year and end-of-year PAHO updates already found. The PAHO Q1 alert would contain independently verified Brazil-specific case and death figures for SE 1–13.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO epidemiological alert or situation report specifically covering the Brazil dengue emergency in Q1 2024 (January–March); expected to contain Brazil national case/death figures for SE 1–13 and possibly subnational hotspot data.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: paho.org domain; PAHO/WHO authorship; date within January–March 2024; 'epidemiological alert' or 'alerta epidemiológico' label.
query_batch.previous_iteration_basis: it1_q2 — PAHO results found were June and October 2024; this query targets the Q1-specific PAHO alert

query_batch.query: dengue São Paulo Minas Gerais Rio de Janeiro 2024 casos óbitos janeiro fevereiro março secretaria saúde boletim
query_batch.query_rationale: São Paulo, Minas Gerais, and Rio de Janeiro were the three highest-burden states in Q1 2024 Brazil dengue outbreak. Iteration 1 returned Minas Gerais (saude.mg.gov.br) and Distrito Federal (saude.df.gov.br) state bulletins, but the snippets indicate these cover later periods (June 2024, SE 52). São Paulo — the most populous state and likely the highest absolute case count — did not appear at all. This query targets Q1-specific state-level bulletins from these three key states to populate the subnational_location and locality fields. Portuguese-language query with state names and month terms maximises recall of state health secretariat publications.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State health secretariat (Secretaria de Estado de Saúde) bulletins or situation reports for São Paulo (saude.sp.gov.br), Minas Gerais (saude.mg.gov.br), and Rio de Janeiro (saude.rj.gov.br) covering dengue cases and deaths in January–March 2024.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: saude.sp.gov.br, saude.mg.gov.br, or saude.rj.gov.br domain; state health secretariat authorship; date within January–March 2024; SE 1–13 reference.

query_batch.query: ProMED Brazil dengue 2024 outbreak cases deaths OR "WHO disease outbreak news" Brazil dengue 2024
query_batch.query_rationale: ProMED-mail posts and WHO Disease Outbreak News (DON) entries provide independently timestamped, peer-reviewed outbreak alerts that are valuable for corroborating official figures and establishing precise event dates. Neither appeared in iteration 1 results despite being expected sources for a record-breaking outbreak. ProMED posts from January–March 2024 would contain quantitative figures cited from Brazilian MoH and PAHO, with precise dates. WHO DON entries, if published, would provide WHO's official characterisation of the emergency. This query uses an OR construction to maximise recall across both channels.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED-mail posts (promedmail.org) or WHO Disease Outbreak News entries (who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news) for Brazil dengue 2024, dated January–March 2024; expected to contain case/death figures with explicit source citations and event dates.
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: promedmail.org domain with post date in Jan–Mar 2024; or who.int/emergencies domain with DON publication date in Q1 2024; explicit citation of Brazilian MoH or PAHO figures.
